abstractExcerpt: While make-on-demand libraries now span trillions of molecules, full library docking struggles beyond a few billion, motivating prioritization that recovers top-scoring compounds while evaluating only a fraction of a library. Here we introduce a similarity-based prioritization approach, ChemSTEP, and define the effective size of a library treated by any prioritization algorithm, Neff. ChemSTEP docks a representative seed set, selects diverse high-scoring “beacons”, and iteratively traverses the library through cycles of beacon selection, similarity search, and docking.

title: Minimal building blocks for molecular quantum circuits with exact spin symmetry
abstractExcerpt: Preserving particle number and spin helps quantum circuits target molecular electronic states, but does not guarantee access to every state with the required quantum numbers. We determine which additional operations, combined with spin-independent orbital rotations connecting all spatial orbitals, generate every real state-space rotation within each complete subspace of fixed particle number $N$, total spin $S$, and spin projection $M_S$.

abstractExcerpt: We describe the staged modernization of a local multilayer TRIM.SP implementation, denoted TRIM.SP-NL. The work included behavior-preserving refactoring, correction of localized bookkeeping and initialization defects, support for more than five elements per layer, reproducible build modes, and a runtime-selectable random-number-generator (RNG) interface. The RANLUX RNG remains the default reference backend, while PCG32 and xoshiro256** provide faster alternatives without changing the input-deck format.

title: Predicting Glass Transition Temperature of Polyimide Homopolymers and Copolymers Using Interpretable QSPR-Based Machine Learning: The MFKit Framework
abstractExcerpt: In this work, we address the problem of predicting the glass transition temperature of polyimides, a class of high-performance engineering thermoplastics, with an emphasis on both homopolymer and copolymer systems. While machine learning approaches have been widely applied to polymer property prediction, their extension to copolymers remains limited and often lacks the interpretability required for rational materials design.

title: Impaired Reinforcement Learning Underlying Explore-Exploit Decision Making in Theft Recidivists
abstractExcerpt: Larceny imposes profound societal and economic burdens; however, punitive judicial measures frequently fail to deter recidivism. The neurobehavioral mechanisms driving habitual offending, whether instrumental or kleptomanic, in theft recidivists remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated explore-exploit decision-making and underlying reinforcement learning architectures in theft recidivists with a 4-arm bandit task while prefrontal cortex (PFC) hemodynamics were continuously monitored using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).

title: Avidity by Design: Scalable Programmed Synthesis of Bivalent DNA-Encoded Libraries for Enhanced Selection Sensitivity
abstractExcerpt: DNA Encoded Libraries (DELs) are used for finding small molecule binders to proteins and other targets of pharmaceutical interest. DELs tether small molecules made by combinatorial chemistry to DNA oligos whose sequences identify the molecules to which they are tethered. DEL selections, or screens, typically separate binders from non-binders and use sequencing to discern binder structures. Typically, selection methods more efficiently capture tighter binders than weaker ones. There are two key reasons why DEL selections may return very few, or no binders.

title: Grammar for Chemically Auditable MOF Adsorption Machine Learning
abstractExcerpt: Machine learning is now routinely used to screen metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), but the object seen by a model is not the crystal itself. Instead, it is a representation: a selected set of geometric, topological, chemical, or learned descriptors that determines which structural evidence can influence prediction, ranking, and candidate selection. Here, we develop a representationcentric audit for MOF adsorption machine learning using a large ARC–MOF-derived cohort with matched CO2 and CH4 uptake targets.

abstractExcerpt: Defect engineering of memristive materials offers a powerful strategy for regulating ionic transport and analog resistive switching required for neuromorphic computing. Here, we report a wet chemical synthesis route for chloride-vacancy (VCl) engineering in lead-free all-inorganic KCuCl3-x thin films and establish a direct correlation between defect concentration, electronic structure, transport dynamics, and neuromorphic performance.

title: A new generation of effective core potentials: Selected heavy 5d and 6p elements

openalex.subfield: Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics

abstractExcerpt: We expand the correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) library by developing semi-local pseudopotentials and matching basis sets by heavy-elements from $5d$ (Hf, Os, Hg) and $6p$ (Tl, Po, At, Rn) blocks. In order to accurately capture scalar relativistic effects, spin-orbit coupling, and electron-electron correlation, we implement a tiered core-valence partitioning strategy across three distinct resolutions.

title: Predictive beam-lattice reduction for higher-order topological modes in a 2D SSH phononic crystal
abstractExcerpt: We develop a mechanically faithful reduced model for a two-dimensional topological phononic crystal composed of rigid square masses connected by slender elastic ligaments. Exploiting Euler Bernoulli beam theory, we derive a Hermitian 12 degree of freedom dynamical matrix that retains in-plane translations, rotations, and ligament eccentricity. This reduction captures effects that are absent from scalar mass spring SSH models while remaining computationally much more tractable and more easily interpretable than full finite element simulations.

title: Matrix-free phase-field modeling of fracture in micromechanical testing simulations of inelastic materials
abstractExcerpt: Resolving steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in the phase-field modeling of fracture favors the use of high-order finite elements, for which matrix-free methods can provide superior performance and scalability. Here, we implement the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework for visco-elastoplastic materials in an open source solid mechanics library supporting matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements with p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs.

title: ChemAgent: A Multi-Agent Attention Framework with Linear Distilled Encoding for Molecular Property Prediction and Chemical Reaction Optimization
abstractExcerpt: Molecular property prediction and chemical reaction optimization are critical for accelerating drug discovery and materials design, yet existing approaches face significant challenges in capturing long-range dependencies, dynamically adapting to molecular characteristics, integrating multi-modal chemical data, and modeling temporal variations in chemical processes. We propose ChemAgent, a unified multi-agent attention framework that addresses these limitations through four synergistic innovations.
